scenes.heading: Choosing your first product to sell

sents.d: Choosing your first product to sell
Validate demand before you build a whole store around it.
Before building a store, look for products with signs of real demand: repeat-purchase potential, gift appeal, or an existing but underserved search volume.
A product nobody is searching for is a much harder sell no matter how good your marketing is.

Check the competitive landscape honestly — some competition confirms demand, but a market flooded with well-funded competitors selling near-identical items at lower prices is a difficult place to start.
Run the numbers on realistic margins (product cost, shipping, payment fees, returns) before committing, since a product that looks exciting can still be unprofitable once real costs are included.

take: Pick a product with proven demand and real margins.
